$comment: The single source of the army's structure. tests/roles.sh validates it against roles/<name>/ROLE.md frontmatter (spawns, tools) and against workflows/*.json (bound roles, step outputs, reachability); bin/fm-workflow validate refuses a step bound to a role whose `outputs` do not include the step's output. spawns: the ONLY roles a role may call through OMP's native bounded task helper (primary policy section 6); every target must itself spawn nothing, so nothing recurses beyond one level. adhoc: why a role is not bound to any workflow step and not a spawn target of a bound role.

senior-fullstack.contract: Ordinary delivery work: the smallest change that fully solves the stated problem, verified by running it.

test-engineer.contract: Writes the verifiers (failing regression, property, differential, end-to-end tests) and proves they fail for the intended reason; never edits production source.

refactorist.contract: One small behavior-preserving improvement, proven by the same checks before and after.

perf-engineer.adhoc: performance tasks are DEEP-category work chosen per task by the Captain; no workflow in this repository is performance-shaped, and the engineering workflows already cover verification of the change itself
perf-engineer.contract: Measure-first optimisation: baseline, one change at a time, keep-or-revert, repeatable evidence with the limiter named.

technical-writer.adhoc: documentation-only tasks change no behavior, so they are not code-changing tasks: the selection kind docs is outside the forcing rule
technical-writer.contract: Scoped documentation of settled behavior or decisions from authoritative source.

chore.adhoc: the trivial/mechanical-chore exception of the forced-workflow rule: fully specified mechanical work needs no workflow
chore.contract: Exactly the mechanical thing the brief spells out, and nothing around it.

lead.adhoc: bound to a workflow's implementer alias by the Captain for one large, already-scoped task with next --role implementer=lead at the start of that task; it never replaces the workflow's independent QA/review steps
lead.contract: Owns one large, already-scoped deliverable inside one task worktree: decomposes, fans bounded slices to sub-agents, integrates, verifies, reports.

planner.contract: Turns an unclear or oversized request into a written spec and an ordered, independently verifiable task list; never implements.

architecture.contract: Structural decisions - boundaries, data models, dependency direction, failure behavior - without owning the implementation.

researcher.contract: Answers a question from high-trust primary sources and returns cited findings with confidence.

scout.contract: Read-only fact gathering over a codebase or a handed PR, reported with evidence and limits; never judges.

debugger.contract: Source-read-only root-cause diagnosis anchored on a red-capable reproduction command; never applies fixes.

risk-classifier.contract: Reads the change and sets its risk tier, whether a security review is required and the diff-triggered checklist items that match.

qa.contract: Independent verification of a change against the task's acceptance by running it; never edits.

ui-qa.contract: Independent verification of browser-visible behavior by driving the real running app, with screenshot/snapshot evidence.

code-reviewer.contract: Read-only review of a handed diff in fresh context: correctness first, severity-tagged findings, each with a failing scenario.

finding-verifier.contract: Tries to disprove each review or security finding before it reaches the implementer; only confirmed findings go back.

security-engineer.contract: Finds, evidences and ranks security weaknesses in a named scope; report-only, never exploits; a blocking gate when asked.

release-engineer.contract: Decides ship-readiness for the head commit and prepares the delivery package (verification stamp, risk, rollback); never pushes or merges.

tenth-man.contract: Deliberate adversarial challenge of a plan, design, diagnosis, finding or completion claim.

improver.adhoc: the self-improvement loop runs on the Captain's cadence over the retro log, never inside a running task; its proposals reach the repository only through a normal PR
improver.contract: Turns recorded failure patterns into proposed role, rule or skill changes through a PR; never self-applies.
